Match the following?

property metal

(b)~Element with highest third ionization enthalpy $\left({Δ}_{i}{H}_{3}\right)$ $( ii ) Cr$

The atomic number of copper is $29$. It has the electronic configuration of~$3d^{10}4s^{1}$. After the first ionisation energy it has the electronic configuration of~$3d^{10}4s^{0}$. After that it has the very high second ionisation energy because of fully filled $d -$orbital. Zinc has the atomic number of the $30$. It has the electronic configuration of~$3d^{10}4s^{2}$. After that~the second ionisation energy it has the electronic configuration of& $3d^{10}4s^{0}$.~After that it has the very high third ionisation energy because of fully filled $d -$orbital. The carbonyl~ligand is two electron donor. The carbonyl ligand follows the eighteen electron rule. So, the electron configuration of metal must be& $d^{6}$. So, this metal is chromium. Hence,~$Cr$~is& $M$~in& $\left[M ( CO{)}_{6}\right]$. The element with high heat of atomisation is nickel.

Hence, the correct matches are~$( a \to iii ) , ( b \to iv ) , ( c \to ii ) , ( d \to v )$.

3832.subject: Chemistry
3832.text:
Which of the following statements are correct?
(i) Inductive effect and resonance effect is possible in chlorobenzene.
(ii) Resonance effect dominates over inductive effect in anisole.
(iii) $p$-nitrobenzoic acid is less acidic than $m$-nitrobenzoic acid.
(iv) Diphenylamine is more basic than aniline.
3832.sol:
(i) The $\mathrm{Cl}$ group activates benzene ring more by resonance effect. $\mathrm{Cl}$ group being more electronegative withdraws electrons from benzene ring and shows - I effect. (ii) The methyl group of ether can donate electrons through inductive effect that is not as strong as electron donation effect to the pi-system. So, resonance effect dominates over inductive effect in anisole.
(iii) $p$-nitrobenzoic acid is more acidic than $m$-nitrobenzoic acid. When both acids donate $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ from $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group, then $p$-nitrobenzoate is more stabilised due to $m$-effect of nitro group at meta position by deactivating the ring. So, statement (iii) is incorrect. (iv) Diphenylamine is less basic than aniline. The lone pair of $\mathrm{N}$-atom in diphenylamine is delocalised on two benzene rings due to which it is less available to donate resulting into decrease in basicity. In aniline, it is delocalised on one benzene ring, so lone pair is more available for donation. Hence, it is more basic. So, statement IV is incorrect.

7096.text: The pole of the straight line $9 x+y-28=0$ with respect to the circle $2 x^2+2 y^2-3 x+5 y-7=0$ is
7096.sol:
Let $(h, k)$ be the pole of the line $9 x+y-28=$ with respect to the circle $x^2+y^2-\frac{3}{2} x+\frac{5}{2} y-\frac{7}{2}=0$. Then, the equation of polar is $\begin{aligned}& \text{ polar is }\\
& \qquad h x+k y-\frac{3}{4}( x+h)+\frac{5}{4}( y+k)-\frac{7}{2}=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x\left( h-\frac{3}{4}\right)+ y\left( k+\frac{5}{4}\right)-\frac{3}{4} h+\frac{5}{4} k-\frac{7}{2}=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x(4 h-3)+y(4 k+5)-3 h+5 k-14=0
\end{aligned} This equation and 9 x+y-28=0$ represent the same line. $\begin{array}{lrr}
\therefore& \frac{4 h-3}{9}=\frac{4 k+5}{1}=\frac{-3 h+5 k-14}{-28}=\lambda \text{ (say) }\\
\Rightarrow h= & \frac{3+9 \lambda}{4}, k=\frac{\lambda-5}{4},-3 h+5 k-14=-28 \lambda \\
\Rightarrow & -3\left(\frac{3+9 \lambda}{4}\right)+5\left(\frac{\lambda-5}{4}\right)-14=-28 \lambda \\
\Rightarrow & -9-27 \lambda+5 \lambda-25-56=-112 \lambda \\
\Rightarrow & -22 \lambda-90=-112 \lambda \\
\Rightarrow & & 90 \lambda=90 \Rightarrow \lambda=1
\end{array} Hence, the pole of the given line is $(3,-1)$.$

10197.sol:
Given parabolas are,
\(y²=32 x \text{ and }x^2=256 y\)
We use a standard result to find equation of common tangent. Equation of tangent common to \(y²=4 a x\) and \(x²=4 b y\) is,
\(b^{1 / 3} y+a^{1 / 3} x+\left(a^2 b²\right)^{1 / 3}=0\)
Here,
$\begin{aligned}& 4 a=32 \Rightarrow a=8 \\
& 4 b=256, \quad b=64
\end{aligned}$
So tangent is,
$\begin{array}{ll}& (64)^{1 / 3} y+(8)^{1 / 3} x+\left(8^2 \times64^2\right)^{1$ / 3}=0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad & 4 y+2 x+64=0
\end{array}

10856.text: A bag contains 6 balls. If 4 balls are drawn at a time and all of them are found to be red, then the probability that exactly 5 of the balls in the bag are red is
10856.sol:
Let us define the following events
$E=$ drawn balls are red. $\quad A=4$ red balls in bag.
$B=5$ red balls in bag.
$C=6$ red balls in bag.
Then, $P(A)=P(B)=P(C)\text{ and } \begin{aligned}$P$\left(\frac{E}{A}\right)$& =$\frac{{ }^4 C_4}{{ }^6 C_4}=\frac{1}{15}$\\
P$\left(\frac{E}{B}\right)$& =$\frac{{ }^5 C_4}{{ }^6 C_4}=\frac{5}{15} \text{$ and }P$\left(\frac{E}{C}\right)=\frac{{ }^6 C_4}{{ }^6 C_4}=\frac{15}{15}
\end{aligned}$By applying Baye's theorem,

$\begin{gathered}$P$\left(\frac{B}{A}\right)=\frac{P(B) \cdot P\left(\frac{E}{B}\right)}{P(A) P\left(\frac{E}{A}\right)+P(B) P\left(\frac{E}{B}\right)+P(C) P\left(\frac{E}{C}\right)}$\\
=$\frac{\frac{5}{15}}{\frac{1}{15}+\frac{5}{15}+\frac{15}{15}}=\frac{5}{21}
\end{gathered}$

14833.text: The specific heat capacities of an ideal gas at the constant pressure and at constant volume are \(620 $\mathrm{Jkg}^{-1} \mathrm{ K}^{-1}$\) and \(420 $\mathrm{Jkg}^{-1} \mathrm{ K}^{-1}$\) respectively. The density of the gas at STP is approximately,
14833.sol:
Given, specific heat capacity of a gas at constant pressure, $C_p=620 \mathrm{ J} \mathrm{ kg}^{-1} \mathrm{ K}^{-1}\)$ and $specific heat capacity of gas at constant volume, \(C_V=420 \mathrm{ J} \mathrm{ kg}^{-1} \mathrm{ K}^{-1}\)
\(\because\) Molar specific heat of gas at constant pressure and constant volume are given by
\(\therefore \quad C_p{ }^{\prime}=m C_p=m(620)\)
and \(\quad C_V{ }^{\prime}=m C_v=m(420)\)
As we know that,
\(\because \quad C_p{ }^{\prime}-C_V{ }^{\prime}=R\)
[Here, \(R\) = universal gas constant]
\begin{aligned}m[620-420] & =R \\
\Rightarrow \quad m & =\frac{R}{200} \qquad \ldots (i)
\end{aligned}\)
Now, ideal gas equation,
\(p V=\mu R T\)
where, \(\mu=\) number of moles of gas
or
\begin{aligned}& p V=R T \quad[\because \text{ for }1 \text{ mole, } \mu=1] \\
& \therefore \quad p m=\rho R T \quad\left[\because \text{ density, } \rho=\frac{m}{V}\right]\\
& 10^5 \times \frac{R}{200}=\rhoR(273) \quad \text{ [From Eq. (i)] }\\
& \rho=1.85 \mathrm{Kg}-\mathrm{m}^{-3}
\end{aligned}$
Hence, the option (d) is correct.

15446.text: A long cylindrical glass vessel has a pinhole of diameter \(0.2 \mathrm{~mm}\) at its bottom. The depth to which the vessel can be lowered vertically in a deep water bath without the water entering into the vessel is (surface tension of water, \(T=0.07 \mathrm{Nm}^{-1}\), acceleration due to gravity, \(g=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}\) )
15446.sol:
Given, diameter of a pinhole, \(d=0.2 \mathrm{~mm}\)
\(\therefore\) radius of pinhole, \(r=\frac{0.2}{2}=0 \mathrm{l} \mathrm{mm}=0 . \mathrm{I} \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}\)
When the hydrostatic pressure is equal to the excess pressure, then water cannot enter the pinhole
Hence, \(h \rho g=\frac{2 T}{r}\)
where, \(h=\) depth up to which cylinder is immersed.
\(\rho=\) density of water
\(T=\) surface tension of water
and \(r=\) radius of a pinhole
\(\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad h & =\frac{2 T}{\rho g r}=\frac{2 \times 0.07}{10^3 \times 10 \times 0.1 \times 10^{-3}} \\
& =0.14 \mathrm{~m}=14 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, the depth to which the vessel can be lowered vertically in a deep water bath without the water entering into the vessel is \(14 \mathrm{~cm}\).

19559.subject: Chemistry
19559.text: Which of the following compounds undergo Aldol condensation followed by dehydration to give 3-phenylprop-2-en-1-al?
options:
Benzaldehyde and Acetone
Two molecules of Benzaldehyde
Benzaldehyde and Ethanal
Benzaldehyde and Acetophenone
19559.sol:
The target product is 3-phenylprop-2-en-1-al, which is cinnamaldehyde. Its structure is $C_{6}H_{5}-CH=CH-CHO$.

The structure contains a phenyl group attached to a three-carbon chain with an aldehyde functional group at the end. This indicates that the condensation occurs between an aromatic aldehyde (benzaldehyde) and an aliphatic aldehyde (ethanal).

The reaction is a Claisen-Schmidt condensation, a type of crossed aldol condensation. Benzaldehyde ($C_{6}H_{5}CHO$) acts as the electrophile because it lacks $\alpha$-hydrogens, and ethanal ($CH_{3}CHO$) acts as the nucleophile because it possesses $\alpha$-hydrogens.

The reaction proceeds as follows: $C_{6}H_{5}CHO + CH_{3}CHO \xrightarrow{OH^{-}} C_{6}H_{5}CH(OH)CH_{2}CHO \xrightarrow{-H_{2}O} C_{6}H_{5}CH=CHCHO$.

Therefore, the reactants are benzaldehyde and ethanal.

Answer: Benzaldehyde and Ethanal

Match $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}$ and D with the appropriate functions given. \(
Column IFunctions

BPhosphodiester bondsQRegulates responses to external stimuli.

Oxidoreductases are enzymes that catalyze oxidation-reduction reactions. In the context of metabolic pathways like glycolysis, enzymes such as glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase act as oxidoreductases. Thus, A matches with R.

Phosphodiester bonds are the covalent linkages that connect the 3' carbon atom of one sugar molecule and the 5' carbon atom of another in the sugar-phosphate backbone of DNA and RNA. Thus, B matches with S.

The adrenal cortex is an endocrine gland that produces essential hormones like cortisol and aldosterone. Malfunctioning or deficiency of the adrenal cortex leads to Addison's disease. Thus, C matches with P.

Epinephrine, also known as adrenaline, is a hormone and neurotransmitter that prepares the body for fight-or-flight responses, effectively regulating responses to external stimuli. Thus, D matches with Q.

Combining these, we get A=R, B=S, C=P, D=Q.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{R} \quad \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{S} \quad \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{P} \quad \mathrm{D}=\mathrm{Q}$

19758.subject: Chemistry
19758.text:
From the given covalent compounds (A to F) identify the pair of molecules which have:
(i) Two lone pairs of electrons on the central atom.
(ii) One lone pair of electrons on the central atom.
A. $\mathrm{SO}_2$
B. $\mathrm{ClF}_3$
C. $\mathrm{BF}_3$
D. $\mathrm{BrF}_5$
E. $\mathrm{XeF}_4$
F. $\mathrm{SF}_6$
options: $(i) A \ \text{ and } F \quad (ii) A \ \text{ and } E$
19758.sol:
The number of lone pairs on the central atom is determined by the formula: Lone pairs = $\dfrac{1}{2}(V - N - C)$, where $V$ is the number of valence electrons of the central atom, $N$ is the number of monovalent atoms bonded to it, and $C$ is the charge on the molecule.

A. $\mathrm{SO}_2$: $V=6$, $N=0$ (oxygen is divalent). Lone pairs = $\dfrac{1}{2}(6 - 0) = 3$ (considering bonding electrons). More accurately, $\mathrm{S}$ has 6 valence electrons, 2 are used for double bonds with each O, leaving 1 lone pair.

B. $\mathrm{ClF}_3$: $V=7$, $N=3$. Lone pairs = $\dfrac{1}{2}(7 - 3) = 2$.

C. $\mathrm{BF}_3$: $V=3$, $N=3$. Lone pairs = $\dfrac{1}{2}(3 - 3) = 0$.

D. $\mathrm{BrF}_5$: $V=7$, $N=5$. Lone pairs = $\dfrac{1}{2}(7 - 5) = 1$.

E. $\mathrm{XeF}_4$: $V=8$, $N=4$. Lone pairs = $\dfrac{1}{2}(8 - 4) = 2$.

F. $\mathrm{SF}_6$: $V=6$, $N=6$. Lone pairs = $\dfrac{1}{2}(6 - 6) = 0$.

Comparing the results:
(i) Two lone pairs: B ($\mathrm{ClF}_3$) and E ($\mathrm{XeF}_4$).
(ii) One lone pair: A ($\mathrm{SO}_2$) and D ($\mathrm{BrF}_5$).

The pair matching (i) is B & E and (ii) is A & D.

Answer: $(i) B \ \text{ and } E \quad (ii) \mathrm{A} \ \text{ and } \mathrm{D}$

21122.subject: Mathematics
21122.text: The equation of a circle passing through the origin is $x^2+y^2-6 x+2 y=0$. The equation of one of its diameter is
21122.sol:
The given equation of the circle is $x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 2y = 0$.

Comparing this with the general equation of a circle $x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$, we have $2g = -6$ and $2f = 2$.

Thus, $g = -3$ and $f = 1$.

The center of the circle is $(-g, -f) = (3,-1)$.

A diameter of a circle is a line passing through its center. Therefore, the equation of the diameter must satisfy the coordinates of the center $(3,-1)$.

Testing the options:

For option (1): $x - 3y = 3 - 3(-1) = 3 + 3 = 6 eq 0$.

For option (2): $x + 3y = 3 + 3(-1) = 3 - 3 = 0$. This satisfies the equation.

For option (3): $x + y = 3 + (-1) = 2 eq 0$.

For option (4): $3x - y = 3(3) - (-1) = 9 + 1 = 10 eq 0$.

Thus, the equation of the diameter is $x + 3y = 0$.

Answer: $x+3 y=0$

21228.subject: Mathematics
21228.text:
$\text{ The function defined by } f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}
\dfrac{\sin x}{x}+\cos x & x> 0 \\
-5 k & x=0 \\
\dfrac{4(1-\sqrt{1-x})}{x} & x< 0
\end{array}$ \quad $\text{$ is continous at } x=0, \quad $\text{$ then } k\right. $\text{ equals }$
21228.sol:
For the function $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x = 0$, the left-hand limit, right-hand limit, and the value of the function at $x = 0$ must be equal.

The right-hand limit is given by $\lim_{x \to 0^{+}} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 0^{+}} \left( \dfrac{\sin x}{x} + \cos x \right) = 1 + 1 = 2$.

The left-hand limit is given by $\lim_{x \to 0^{-}} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 0^{-}} \dfrac{4(1 - \sqrt{1 - x})}{x}$.

Multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $(1 + \sqrt{1 - x})$:

$\lim_{x \to 0^{-}} \dfrac{4(1 - \sqrt{1 - x})(1 + \sqrt{1 - x})}{x(1 + \sqrt{1 - x})} = \lim_{x \to 0^{-}} \dfrac{4(1 - (1 - x))}{x(1 + \sqrt{1 - x})} = \lim_{x \to 0^{-}} \dfrac{4x}{x(1 + \sqrt{1 - x})} = \lim_{x \to 0^{-}} \dfrac{4}{1 + \sqrt{1 - x}} = \dfrac{4}{1 + 1} = 2$.

Since the limit exists and is equal to $2$, we set the value of the function at $x = 0$ equal to this limit:

$-5k = 2$.

Therefore, $k = -\dfrac{2}{5}$.

Answer: $-\dfrac{2}{5}$

23232.subject: Physics
23232.text: Rain is falling vertically downwards at a velocity $9 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$. And wind starts blowing at a speed of $4 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$ in the west to east direction. In which direction should the girl hold her umbrella to protect herself from the rain?
23232.sol:
Let the velocity of rain be $\vec{v}_{r} = -9 \hat{j} \text{ ms}^{-1}$, where $\hat{j}$ is the unit vector in the upward vertical direction.

The velocity of the wind is $\vec{v}_{w} = 4 \hat{i} \text{ ms}^{-1}$, where $\hat{i}$ is the unit vector in the west to east direction.

The velocity of the rain with respect to the girl (who is assumed to be stationary) is $\vec{v}_{rg} = \vec{v}_{r} - \vec{v}_{w} = -4 \hat{i} - 9 \hat{j} \text{ ms}^{-1}$.

To protect herself from the rain, the girl must hold the umbrella in the direction of the relative velocity of the rain, which is $\vec{v}_{rg} = -4 \hat{i} - 9 \hat{j}$.

The angle $\theta$ that the umbrella makes with the vertical is given by $\tan \theta = \dfrac{|v_{x}|}{|v_{y}|} = \dfrac{4}{9}$.

Calculating the value, $\tan \theta = 0.444... \approx 0.44$.

Since the horizontal component of the relative velocity is $-4 \hat{i}$ (directed towards the west), the girl must tilt the umbrella towards the west to counter the rain coming from the east.

Answer: $\theta=\tan ^{-1}(0.44)$ with the vertical towards west

25473.text: For $x \in \mathbb{R}$, let the function $y\left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 12y = cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}x\right), y\left(0\right) = 0 .$ Then, which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
options: There exists a real number $\beta$ such that the line $y = \beta$ intersects the curve $y = y\left(x\right)$ at infinitely many points
25473.sol:
Given,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 12y = cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{12}\right)$

$I . F = {e}^{12x}$

Now solution of the differential equation is given by,

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{12x} = ∫ {e}^{12x} \cdot cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{12}\right)dx + C$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{12x} = \dfrac{{e}^{12x}}{{12}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)}^{2}}\left[12cos\dfrac{\pix}{12} + \dfrac{\pi}{12}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{12}\right)\right] + C$

Now given curve is passing through $\left(0, 0\right)$

So, $y\left(0\right) = 0 ⇒ C = - \dfrac{12}{{12}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)}^{2}}$

So $y = \dfrac{1}{\lambda}\left[\mathop{\mathop{12cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{12}\right) + \dfrac{\pi}{12}sin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{12}\right)}_{⏟}}_{{f}_{1}\left(x\right)} - 12{e}^{- 12x}\right]$

{Where $\lambda = \dfrac{1}{{12}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)}^{2}}$ }

Now on differentiating we get,

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}^{'}}\left[\mathop{\mathop{- \pisin\left(\dfrac{\pix}{12}\right) + \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{{12}^{2}}cos\left(\dfrac{\pix}{12}\right)}_{⏟}}_{{f}_{2}\left(x\right)} + 12{e}^{- 12x}\right]$

$\left\{\text{where}{\lambda}^{'} = \dfrac{12}{{12}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)}^{2}}\right\}$

Now when $x$ is large then $12{e}^{- 12x}$ tends to zero.

But ${f}_{2}\left(x\right)$ varies in $\left[- \sqrt{{\pi}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)}^{4}}, \sqrt{{\pi}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)}^{4}}\right]$ $\left\{\text{by using} - \sqrt{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2}} \text{ and } \sqrt{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2}}\right\}$

Hence $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is changing its sign.

So $y\left(x\right)$ is non monotonic for all real number.
Also when $x$ is very large then again $- 12{e}^{- 12x}$ is almost zero but ${f}_{1}\left(x\right)$ is periodic, so there exist some $\beta$ for which $y = \beta$ intersect $y = y\left(x\right)$ at infinitely many points.

26379.text:
A cylindrical furnace has height $\left(H\right)$ and diameter $\left(D\right)$ both $1m$. It is maintained at temperature $360K$. The air gets heated inside the furnace at constant pressure ${P}_{a}$ and its temperature becomes $T = 360K$. The hot air with density $ρ$ rises up a vertical chimney of diameter $d = 0 . 1m$ and height $h = 9m$ above the furnace and exits the chimney (see the figure). As a result, atmospheric air of density ${ρ}_{a} = 1 . 2kg{m}^{- 3}$, pressure ${P}_{a}$ and temperature ${T}_{a} = 300K$ enters the furnace. Assume air as an ideal gas, neglect the variations in $ρ and T$ inside the chimney and the furnace. Also ignore the viscous effects.

[Given: The acceleration due to gravity $g = 10m{s}^{- 2} and \pi = 3 . 14$]


Considering the air flow to be streamline, the steady mass flow rate of air exiting the chimney is _____ $gm{s}^{- 1}$.
26379.sol:
Applying Bernoulli’s theorem between top and bottom points of furnace :

${P}_{a} + \dfrac{1}{2}{ρ}_{a}{V}^{2} = {P}_{a} + ρgH + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

Also, since $PM = ρRT$

$⇒ {ρ}_{a} \times 300 = ρ \times 360$

$⇒ ρ = 1kg{m}^{- 3} . . . \left(2\right)$

From equation(1), we can write

$⇒ \dfrac{{V}^{2}}{2}\left(0 . 2\right) = 1 \times 10 \times 1$

$⇒ V = 10m{s}^{- 1}$

Required mass flow rate $= V \times \dfrac{\pi{D}^{2}}{4} \times ρ$

$= 10 \times \dfrac{3 . 14}{4} \times {1}^{2} \times 1kg{s}^{- 1}$

$= 7 . 85kg{s}^{- 1}$

$= 7850gm{s}^{- 1}$

30665.text: Hydrogen has three isotopes : protium $\left(H 1\right)$, deuterium ($H 2 or D$) and tritium ($H 3 or T$). They have nearly same chemical properties but different physical properties. They differ in
30665.sol:
Isotopes are the atoms of the same element with different mass number. They have the same atomic number. So, number of protons and electrons are same, Hence their electronic configuration are same, but number of neutrons are different.

Hydrogen has three isotopes: protium, $H 11$, deuterium, $H 12$ or $D$ and tritium, $H 13$ or $T$. These isotopes differ from one another in respect of the presence of neutrons. Ordinary hydrogen, protium, has no neutrons, deuterium (also known as heavy hydrogen) has one and tritium has two neutrons in the nucleus.

32413.subject: Chemistry
32413.text:
The number of colloidal systems from the following, which will have 'liquid' as the dispersion medium, is _____.

Gem stones, paints, smoke, cheese, milk, hair cream, insecticide sprays, froth, soap lather
32413.sol:
The phase that is scattered or present in the form of colloidal particles is called dispersed phase and the medium in which the colloidal particles are dispersed is called the dispersion medium.

Coloured gemstones are solid sols, colloids in which solid particles are dispersed in solid medium. In paints, small amount of solid pigments are dispersed in a large amount of liquid solvent. So, it is an example of a solid in liquid mixture. Smoke is a solid aerosol-type colloid consisting of the solid dispersed phase in the gaseous dispersed medium. Cheese is an example of gel in the colloidal systems, in which the dispersed phase is a liquid while the dispersion medium is a solid. Milk is a type of 'liquid in liquid' colloid, also known as emulsion. Hair cream is an example of a colloidal system where dispersed Phase is Liquid and dispersion Medium is also Liquid. Insecticide sprays is an example of a colloidal solution in which liquid particles are dispersed in the gaseous phase. Froth is a colloidal solution of gas in liquid. Soap lather is an example of colloidal system foam in which the dispersed phase is gas and the dispersion medium is liquid.

Paints, milk, froth, soap lather and hair cream have liquid as dispersion medium.

32546.subject: Chemistry
32546.text: Which of the following graphs between pressure ' p ' versus volume ' V ' represents the maximum work done?
32546.sol:
In a pressure-volume ($P-V$) graph, the magnitude of work done is represented by the area under the curve bounded by the volume axis.
Let's analyze the area under the curve for each graph:
Graph (1) represents an expansion from $V = 22.4$ L to $V = 44.8$ L. The area is the integral $\int_{22.4}^{44.8} P dV$, which covers a significant region under the curve.
Graph (2) represents a cyclic process. The net work done is the area enclosed by the loop. This area is much smaller than the total area under the expansion curve in graph (1).
Graph (3) represents an isochoric process (constant volume $V = 22.4$ L). Since $dV = 0$, the work done $W = \int P dV = 0$.
Graph (4) also represents a cyclic process. Similar to graph (2), the net work done is the area enclosed by the loop, which is smaller than the area under the expansion curve in graph (1).
Comparing all cases, the expansion process in graph (1) covers the maximum area under the $P-V$ curve, thus representing the maximum work done.

35496.text: Let $I\left(x\right) = ∫ \sqrt{\dfrac{x + 7}{x}}dx$ and $I\left(9\right) = 12 + 7{\log}_{e}7$. If $I\left(1\right) = \alpha + 7{\log}_{e}\left(1 + 2\sqrt{2}\right),$ then ${\alpha}^{4}$ is equal to _____.
35496.sol:
Given,

$I\left(x\right) = ∫ \sqrt{\dfrac{x + 7}{x}}dx$

Now let, $\dfrac{x + 7}{x} = {t}^{2} ⇒ - \dfrac{7}{{x}^{2}}dx = 2tdt$

$⇒ dx = \dfrac{- 14t}{{\left({t}^{2} - 1\right)}^{2}}dt$

So, $I\left(x\right) = - 14 ∫ \dfrac{{t}^{2}}{{\left({t}^{2} - 1\right)}^{2}}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = - 14 ∫ \dfrac{dt}{\left({t}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}} - 2\right)}$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 14}{2} ∫ \left[\dfrac{\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}\right)}{{\left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)}^{2} - 4} + \dfrac{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}\right)}{{\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right)}^{2}}\right]dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = - 7\left(\dfrac{1}{4}ln\left|\dfrac{t + \dfrac{1}{t} - 2}{t + \dfrac{1}{t} + 2}\right| - \dfrac{1}{t - \dfrac{1}{t}}\right) + c$

Now when $x = 9, t = \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ I\left(9\right) = 12 + 7 \times ln7 = \dfrac{- 7}{4}ln{\left(\dfrac{1}{7}\right)}^{2} + 7 \times \dfrac{12}{7} + c$

$⇒ c = \dfrac{7}{2}ln7$

Now when $x = 1, t = 2\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ I\left(1\right) = + \dfrac{7}{4}ln{\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{2} + 1}{2\sqrt{2} - 1}\right)}^{2} + 7 \times \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{7} + \dfrac{7}{2}ln7$

$⇒ I\left(1\right) = \dfrac{7}{2}ln\left(\dfrac{{\left(2\sqrt{2} + 1\right)}^{2}}{7}\right) + 2\sqrt{2} + \dfrac{7}{2}ln7$

$⇒ I\left(1\right) = 7ln\left(2\sqrt{2} + 1\right) - \dfrac{7}{2}ln7 + 2\sqrt{2} + \dfrac{7}{2}ln7$

$⇒ \alpha = 2\sqrt{2} ⇒ {\alpha}^{4} = 64$

35579.subject: Mathematics
35579.text: If $\sin(\tan^{-1}(x\sqrt{2})) = \cot(\sin^{-1}\sqrt{1-x^2})$, $x \in (0,1)$, then the value of $x$ is :
35579.sol:
Let $\alpha = \tan^{-1}(x\sqrt{2}) \Rightarrow \tan\alpha = x\sqrt{2}$

From the right-angled triangle, $\sin\alpha = \dfrac{x\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{1+2x^2}}$

Let $\beta = \sin^{-1}\sqrt{1-x^2} \Rightarrow \sin\beta = \sqrt{1-x^2}$

From the right-angled triangle, $\cos\beta = \sqrt{1 - (1-x^2)} = x$

$\cot\beta = \dfrac{\cos\beta}{\sin\beta} = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$

Given $\sin\alpha = \cot\beta$, substituting the values:

$\dfrac{x\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{1+2x^2}} = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$

Since $x \in (0,1)$, $x \neq 0$. Dividing by $x$ and squaring both sides:

$\dfrac{2}{1+2x^2} = \dfrac{1}{1-x^2}$

$2(1-x^2) = 1+2x^2$

$2 - 2x^2 = 1 + 2x^2$

$4x^2 = 1$

$x^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Since $x \in (0,1)$, $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}$

36107.text: If $A = \left[\begin{cases}0 & - tan\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) \\ tan\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) & 0\end{cases}\right]$ and $\left({I}_{2} + A\right){\left({I}_{2} - A\right)}^{- 1} = \left[\begin{cases}a & - b \\ b & a\end{cases}\right],$ then $13\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2}\right)$ is equal to _____ .

$⇒ {\left(I - A\right)}^{- 1} = \dfrac{1}{{sec}^{2}\dfrac{\theta}{2}}\left[\begin{cases}1 & - tan\dfrac{\theta}{2} \\ tan\dfrac{\theta}{2} & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left(I + A\right){\left(I - A\right)}^{- 1} = \dfrac{1}{{sec}^{2}\dfrac{\theta}{2}}\left[\begin{cases}1 & - tan\dfrac{\theta}{2} \\ tan\dfrac{\theta}{2} & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & - tan\dfrac{\theta}{2} \\ tan\dfrac{\theta}{2} & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{{sec}^{2}\dfrac{\theta}{2}}\left[\begin{cases}1 - \tan^{2}\dfrac{\theta}{2} & - 2tan\dfrac{\theta}{2} \\ 2tan\dfrac{\theta}{2} & 1 - \tan^{2}\dfrac{\theta}{2}\end{cases}\right]$

37160.subject: Mathematics
37160.text: Let ${a}_{1}, {a}_{2}, {a}_{3}, \ldots$ be an A.P. If $\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{\infty}\dfrac{{a}_{r}}{{2}^{r}} = 4$, then $4{a}_{2}$ is equal to ______.
37160.sol:
Let $S = \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{\infty}\dfrac{{a}_{r}}{{2}^{r}}$

$⇒ S = \dfrac{{a}_{1}}{2} + \dfrac{{a}_{2}}{{2}^{2}} + \dfrac{{a}_{3}}{{2}^{3}} + \ldots . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{S}{2} = \dfrac{{a}_{1}}{{2}^{2}} + \dfrac{{a}_{2}}{{2}^{3}} + \ldots . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Now subtracting both equation we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{S}{2} = \dfrac{{a}_{1}}{2} + d\left(\dfrac{1}{{2}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{2}^{3}} + \ldots\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{S}{2} = \dfrac{{a}_{1}}{2} + d\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{4}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}}\right)$

$⇒ S = {a}_{1} + d = {a}_{2}$

Now given $S = \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{\infty}\dfrac{{a}_{r}}{{2}^{r}} = 4$

So, $S = {a}_{2} = 4$

So, $4{a}_{2} = 16$

Let W denote the words in the English dictionary. Define the relation R by :
$R=\{(x, y) \in W \times W \mid$ the words $x$ and $y$ have at least one letter in common $\}$. Then $R$ is
options:
not reflexive, symmetric and transitive

reflexive, symmetric and not transitive

reflexive, symmetric and transitive

reflexive, not symmetric and transitive
37490.sol:
Clearly $(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{x}) \in \mathrm{R} \forall \mathrm{x} \in \mathrm{W}$. So, $\mathrm{R}$ is reflexive.
Let $(x, y) \in R$, then $(y, x) \in R$ as $x$ and $y$ have at least one letter in common. So, $R$ is symmetric.
But $R$ is not transitive for example
Let $x=$ DELHI, $y=$ DWARKA and $z=$ PARK
then $(x, y) \in R$ and $(y, z) \in R$ but $(x, z) \notin R$.

Here, $\overset{\to}{AB} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{MN} = \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 1 & - 2 \\ 2 & - 3 & 2\end{cases}\right| = - 4\overset{^}{i} - 8\overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{AB} \cdot \overset{\to}{MN} = - 12 - 80 - 16 = - 108$

38199.text:
The direction ratios of normal to the plane through the

points (0,-1,0) and (0,0,1) and making an angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$

with the plane $y-z+5=0$ are;

2,-1,1

$2, \sqrt{2}-\sqrt{2}$

$\sqrt{2}, 1,-1$

$2 \sqrt{3}, 1,-1$
38199.sol:
Let the d.r's of the normal be $\langle a, b, c\rangle$ Equation of the plane is $a(x-0)+b(y+1)+c(z-0)=0$

$\because$ It passes through (0,0,1)

$\therefore \quad b+c=0$

Also $\frac{0 \cdot a+b-c}{\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2} \cdot \sqrt{2}}}=\cos \frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \quad b-c=\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}}$

And $b+c=0$

$\Rightarrow \quad b=\pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} a$

$\therefore \quad$ The d.r's are $\sqrt{2}, 1,-1$ or $2, \sqrt{2},-\sqrt{2}$

38818.text: To light, a $50W, 100V$ lamp is connected, in series with a capacitor of capacitance $\dfrac{50}{\pi\sqrt{x}}\muF$, with $200V, 50HzAC$ source. The value of $x$ will be _____ .
38818.sol:
Electrical power is given by $P = \dfrac{{V}^{2}}{R} ⇒ R = \dfrac{{V}^{2}}{P}$

Resistance of lamp is $R = \dfrac{100 \times 100}{50} ⇒ R = 200Ω$

Let ${V}_{C}$ and ${V}_{R}$ be the voltage across capacitor and resistor.

Here, ${V}_{R}^{2} + {V}_{C}^{2} = {V}^{2}$

Current through lamp is $i = \dfrac{100}{200} = \dfrac{1}{2}A$

$⇒ {\left(100\right)}^{2} + {V}_{C}^{2} = {\left(200\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {V}_{C}^{2} = 30000 ⇒ {V}_{C} = 100\sqrt{3}V$

We know that, $V = i \times {X}_{C}$

Then, ${X}_{C} = 200\sqrt{3}Ω = \dfrac{1}{\omega C}$

So, capacitance of capacitor is $C = \dfrac{1}{20 \times 50 \times 20\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{50 \times {10}^{- 6}}{\sqrt{x}}$

$\sqrt{x} = 50 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 100 \times 200\sqrt{3}$

Thus, value of $x = 3$.

40765.text:
In an experiment to find out the diameter of wire using screw gauge, the following observation were noted:

(a) Screw moves $0 . 5mm$ on main scale in one complete rotation
(b) Total divisions on circular scale $= 50$
(c) Main scale reading is $2 . 5mm$
(d) ${45}^{th}$ division of circular scale is in the pitch line
(e) Instrument has $0 . 03mm$ negative error Then the diameter of wire is :
40765.sol:
From the data given in the question,

Pitch of the screw gauge$= 0 . 5mm$.

Total divisions on the circular scale$n = 50$.

Therefore, the least count of the screw gauge is $LC = \dfrac{\text{pitch}}{n} = \dfrac{0 . 5}{50} = 0 . 01mm$

Now, $MSR = 2 . 5mm$, $CSR = 45$

Diameter reading $=$$MSR + LC \times CSR -$ zero error

$⇒ d = 2 . 5 + 0 . 45 - \left(- 0 . 03\right)$

$⇒ d = 2 . 98mm$

40850.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The angular speed of the moon in its orbit about the earth is more than the angular speed of the earth in its orbit about the sun.
Reason (R): The moon takes less time to move around the earth than the time taken by the earth to move around the sun.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of A.
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of A.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
40850.sol:
It is known that

$\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} ⇒ \omega ∝ \dfrac{1}{T}$

As,
${T}_{\text{moon}} \approx 27$ days
${T}_{\text{earth}} \approx 365$ days
$⇒ {\omega}_{\text{moon}} > {\omega}_{\text{earth}}$

Hence, Both the assertion and the reason are correct and the reason is the correct explanation for the assertion.

41969.text:
The velocity of a small ball of mass $0 . 3g$ and density $8g{cc}^{- 1}$ when dropped in a container filled with glycerine becomes constant after some time. If the density of glycerine is $1 . 3g{cc}^{- 1}$, then the value of viscous force acting on the ball will be $x \times {10}^{- 4}N$, the value of $x$ is _____ .

[use $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$]
41969.sol:
Let ${F}_{V}$ be the viscous force and ${F}_{B}$ be the buoyant force acting on the ball.

​​​​​​​

Then, when body moves with constant velocity,

${F}_{V} + {F}_{B} = Mg$

Or, ${F}_{V} = Mg - {F}_{B}$

${F}_{V} = {ρ}_{B}Vg - {ρ}_{L}Vg$ $= \left({ρ}_{B} -\right)\left({ρ}_{L}\right)Vg$, where, $V$ is the volume of small ball.

$= \left(8 - 1 . 3\right) × {10}^{3} × \dfrac{0 . 3 × {10}^{- 3}}{8 × {10}^{3}} × 10$

$= \dfrac{6 . 7 × 0 . 3}{8} × {10}^{- 2}$

$= \dfrac{67 × 3}{8} × {10}^{- 4} = 25 . 125 × {10}^{- 4} = 25 × {10}^{- 4}N$

Thus, the value of $x = 25$.

42544.text: Substance $A$ has atomic mass number $16$ and half life of $1$ day. Another substance $B$ has atomic mass number $32$ and half life of $\dfrac{1}{2}$ day. If both $A$ and $B$ simultaneously start undergo radio activity at the same time with initial mass $320g$ each, how many total atoms of $A$ and $B$ combined would be left after $2$ days
42544.sol:
Number of nuclei left after n half-lives is given by,

$N = {N}_{0}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\dfrac{t}{{t}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}}$.

As, ${\left({N}_{0}\right)}_{A} = \dfrac{320}{16} = 20moles$ and

${\left({N}_{0}\right)}_{B} = \dfrac{320}{32} = 10moles$

Then, ${N}_{A} = \dfrac{{\left({N}_{0}\right)}_{A}}{{\left(2\right)}^{\dfrac{2}{1}}} = \dfrac{20}{4} = 5$ and

${N}_{B} = \dfrac{{\left({N}_{0}\right)}_{B}}{{\left(2\right)}^{\dfrac{2}{0 . 5}}} = \dfrac{10}{{2}^{4}} = 0 . 625$

So total $N = 5 . 625$

and number of atoms $= 5 . 625 \times 6 . 023 \times {10}^{23}$

$= 3 . 38 \times {10}^{24}$

42716.text: A block of mass $2kg$ is attached with two identical springs of spring constant $20N{m}^{- 1}$ each. The block is placed on a frictionless surface and the ends of the springs are attached to rigid supports (see figure). When the mass is displaced from its equilibrium position, it executes a simple harmonic motion. The time period of oscillation is $\dfrac{\pi}{\sqrt{X}}$ in SI unit. The value of $X$ is______.
42716.sol:
When the block is displaced by a distance $x$, force acting on block due to both springs will be in the same direction. Therefore,

$F = - 2kx ⇒ a = - \dfrac{2k}{m}x,$

Comparing it with$a = - {\omega}^{2}x$ , we get

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{2k}{m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 20}{2}}$

$= \sqrt{20}rad{s}^{- 1}$

Now, $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\sqrt{20}} = \dfrac{\pi}{\sqrt{5}}$

Hence, required value of $X = 5$.

43225.text: A solid sphere is rolling on a horizontal plane without slipping. If the ratio of angular momentum about axis of rotation of the sphere to the total energy of moving sphere is $\pi: 22$ then, the value of its angular speed will be$_________rad{s}^{- 1} .$
43225.sol:
The angular momentum is given by

$L = {I}_{CM}\omega = \dfrac{2M{R}^{2}\omega}{5}$

The total kinetic energy is

$E = \dfrac{1}{2} ( M{v}^{2} + \dfrac{2M{R}^{2}{\omega}^{2}}{5} )$

The ratio of angular momentum and kinetic energy is

$\dfrac{L}{E} = \dfrac{{I}_{CM}\omega}{\dfrac{1}{2}M{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{2}{5}M{R}^{2}{\omega}^{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2}{5}M{R}^{2}\omega}{\dfrac{7}{10}M{R}^{2}{\omega}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\pi}{22} = \dfrac{4}{7} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\omega}$$⇒ \omega = 4rad{s}^{- 1}$

Therefore,

$\dfrac{{R}_{1}}{{R}_{2}} = \dfrac{20}{4} = \dfrac{5}{1}$

44246.text: In Young's double slit experiment, light from two identical sources are superimposing on a screen. The path difference between the two lights reaching at a point on the screen is $\dfrac{7\lambda}{4}$. The ratio of intensity of fringe at this point with respect to the maximum intensity of the fringe is:
44246.sol:
Given the path difference is $∆ x = \dfrac{7\lambda}{4}$

Hence, the phase difference can be found as follows:

$\begin{cases}ϕ & = & \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} ∆ x \\ & = & \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times \dfrac{7\lambda}{4} \\ & = & \dfrac{7\pi}{2}\end{cases}$

The formula to calculate the intensity is given by

$I = {I}_{max}\cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{ϕ}{2}\right) . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{I}{{I}_{max}} & = & \cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{ϕ}{2}\right) \\ & = & \cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{2 \times 2}\right) \\ & = & \cos^{2}\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{4}\right) \\ & = & \cos^{2}\left(2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) \\ & = & \cos^{2}\dfrac{\pi}{4} \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{2}\end{cases}$

\end{aligned}$

We have, $c_{1} y=\left(c_{2}+c_{3}\right) e^{x+c_{4}}\begin{aligned}
&\Rightarrow \quad y=\left(\frac{c_{2}+c_{3}}{c_{1}}\right) e^{c_{4}} \cdot e^{x} \\
&\Rightarrow \quad y=c e^{x} \text{ where } c=\frac{c_{2}+c_{3}}{c_{1}} e^{c_{4}}
\end{aligned}$
Taking log on both sides, we get
$\begin{aligned}
&\log y=\log \left(c e^{x}\right) \\
&\Rightarrow \quad \log y=\log c+x \log e \\
&\Rightarrow \quad \log y=\log c+x \\
&\text{ On differentiating w.r.t.x, we get } \\
&\frac{1}{y} \frac{d y}{d x}=1 \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=y \\
&\therefore \text{ order }=1
\end{aligned}$

55277.text: What is the number of moles of H atoms required for complete reduction of one mole acetonitrile?
55277.sol:
Reduction of acetonitrile follows the general catalytic hydrogenation reaction for nitriles: $R-C\equiv N + 2H_2 \xrightarrow{\text{catalyst}} R-CH_2NH_2$.

For acetonitrile (CH_3CN$): $CH_3-C\equiv N + 2H_2 \rightarrow CH_3CH_2NH_2$.

Each mole of $H_2$ contains 2 moles of hydrogen atoms, so 2 moles of $H_2$ yield 2 \times 2 = 4$ moles of H atoms.

The complete reduction of one mole of acetonitrile requires 4 moles of H atoms.

57143.subject: Chemistry
57143.text: Which from following compounds is NOT optically active?
57143.sol:
The optical activity of a compound depends on the presence of a chiral carbon atom, which is bonded to four different groups.

In 3-bromohexane, the C3 carbon is bonded to a hydrogen atom, a bromine atom, an ethyl group, and a propyl group. Since all four groups are different, it is chiral and optically active.

In 2-bromo-2-methylbutane, the C2 carbon is bonded to a bromine atom, an ethyl group, and two identical methyl groups. Since two groups are the same, it does not have a chiral center and is optically inactive.

In 2-bromopentane, the C2 carbon is bonded to a hydrogen atom, a bromine atom, a methyl group, and a propyl group. It is chiral and optically active.

In 2-bromo-3-methylbutane, the C2 carbon is bonded to a hydrogen atom, a bromine atom, a methyl group, and an isopropyl group. It is chiral and optically active.

Thus, 2-bromo-2-methylbutane is not optically active.

Answer: 2 - Bromo - 2 - methylbutane

Hydrogen peroxide (H_2O_2$) decomposes into water and oxygen gas upon standing or heating.

To prevent or slow down this decomposition, certain substances are added which act as negative catalysts (inhibitors).

Glycerol, along with urea and acetanilide, is commonly used as a stabilizer for hydrogen peroxide. It acts as a negative catalyst and retards the decomposition process.

Therefore, glycerol reduces the reaction rate of the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide.

58623.sol:
Balancing the half-reaction $\mathrm{BiO}_3^{-} + 6\mathrm{H}^{+} + x \mathrme^{-} \to \mathrm{Bi}^{3+} + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ reveals that $x = 2$ through charge conservation or oxidation state analysis.

The oxidation state of bismuth decreases from $+5$ in $\mathrm{BiO}_3^{-}$ to $+3$ in $\mathrm{Bi}^{3+}$, indicating a gain of 2 electrons.

Charge balancing confirms this result: the reactant side charge $(-1 + 6 - x)$ must equal the product side charge $(+3)$, yielding $5 - x = 3$ and thus $x = 2$.

Final answer: $\boxed{2}$

60213.subject: Mathematics
60213.text: The point on the curve $9y^2 = x^3$ where the normal to the curve makes equal intercepts with the co-ordinate axes is
60213.sol:
The equation of the given curve is $9y^2 = x^3$.

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we get:
$18y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2$
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{3x^2}{18y} = \dfrac{x^2}{6y}$

The slope of the normal to the curve is given by $-\dfrac{dx}{dy}$:
Slope of normal = $-\dfrac{6y}{x^2}$

Since the normal makes equal intercepts with the coordinate axes, its slope must be $-1$.
$-\dfrac{6y}{x^2} = -1$
$x^2 = 6y \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{x^2}{6}$

Substituting $y = \dfrac{x^2}{6}$ into the equation of the curve $9y^2 = x^3$, we get:
$9\left(\dfrac{x^2}{6}\right)^2 = x^3$
$9 \times \dfrac{x^4}{36} = x^3$
$\dfrac{x^4}{4} = x^3$
$x^4 - 4x^3 = 0$
$x^3(x - 4) = 0$

For a non-zero intercept, $x \neq 0$, so we have $x = 4$.

Substituting $x = 4$ into $y = \dfrac{x^2}{6}$:
$y = \dfrac{4^2}{6} = \dfrac{16}{6} = \dfrac{8}{3}$

Thus, the required point on the curve is $\left(4, \dfrac{8}{3}\right)$.

Answer: $\left(4, \dfrac{8}{3}\right)$

61275.subject: Mathematics
61275.text: The equation of the curve whose slope is $\dfrac{y-1}{x^2+x}$ and which passes through the point $(1, 0)$ is
61275.sol:
The slope of the curve is given by $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$.

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y-1}{x^2+x}$

Separating the variables, we get:

$\dfrac{dy}{y-1} = \dfrac{dx}{x(x+1)}$

Integrating both sides:

$\int \dfrac{dy}{y-1} = \int \left( \dfrac{1}{x} - \dfrac{1}{x+1} \right) dx$

$\ln|y-1| = \ln|x| - \ln|x+1| + \ln|C|$

$\ln|y-1| = \ln\left|\dfrac{Cx}{x+1}\right|$

$y-1 = \dfrac{Cx}{x+1}$

Since the curve passes through the point $(1, 0)$, we substitute $x = 1$ and $y = 0$:

$0 - 1 = \dfrac{C(1)}{1+1}$

$-1 = \dfrac{C}{2} \Rightarrow C = -2$

Substituting $C = -2$ back into the equation:

$y-1 = \dfrac{-2x}{x+1}$

$(y-1)(x+1) = -2x$

$xy + y - x - 1 = -2x$

$xy + x + y - 1 = 0$

Answer: $xy + x + y - 1 = 0$

62970.subject: Mathematics
62970.text: If the truth value of the statement pattern $[\mathrm{p} \wedge \sim \mathrm{r}] \rightarrow \sim \mathrm{r} \wedge \mathrm{q}$ is False, then which of the following has truth value False?
62970.sol:
Given the statement $S = [p \wedge \sim r] \rightarrow (\sim r \wedge q)$ with truth value False, determine which of the provided options also evaluates to False.

An implication $A \rightarrow B$ is false only when $A$ is true and $B$ is false. Therefore:

$p \wedge \sim r$ must be true, which requires both $p$ and $\sim r$ to be true, so $p \equiv T$ and $r \equiv F$.

Since $\sim r \wedge q$ must be false and $\sim r \equiv T$, it follows that $T \wedge q$ is false only if $q \equiv F$.

Truth values: $p \equiv T$, $q \equiv F$, $r \equiv F$.

Evaluating the options:

Option A: $(p \vee r) \rightarrow \sim r$ becomes $(T \vee F) \rightarrow T$, which simplifies to $T \rightarrow T$ and is true.

Option B: $(r \vee q) \rightarrow \sim p$ becomes $(F \vee F) \rightarrow F$, or $F \rightarrow F$, which is true.

Option C: $\sim(p \vee q) \rightarrow \sim r$ becomes $\sim(T \vee F) \rightarrow T$, or $F \rightarrow T$, which is true.

Option D: $\sim(r \vee q) \rightarrow \sim p$ becomes $\sim(F \vee F) \rightarrow F$, or $T \rightarrow F$, which is false.

Only option D has truth value False.

Final answer: $\boxed{D}$

62981.sol:
The lamp illuminates when the circuit path evaluates to logical '1'. The equivalence of circuits is determined by their simplified Boolean expressions, where series switches combine via AND and parallel via OR.

Circuit (A): The top branch has $S_1$ and $S_2$ in series, and the bottom branch has $S_1$ and $S_3$ in series, with both branches in parallel. The expression is $(S_1 \cdot S_2) + (S_1 \cdot S_3)$, which simplifies to $S_1 \cdot (S_2 + S_3)$ by the distributive property.

Circuit (B): $S_1$ and $S_2$ are in parallel, giving $S_1 + S_2$.

Circuit (C): $S_1$ in series with the parallel combination of $S_2$ and $S_3$, yielding $S_1 \cdot (S_2 + S_3)$.

Circuit (D): All switches in series: $S_1 \cdot S_2 \cdot S_3$.

Circuit (E): $S_3$ in parallel with the series of $S_1$ and $S_2$, giving $S_1 \cdot S_2 + S_3$.

Circuits (A) and (C) share the same simplified expression $S_1 \cdot (S_2 + S_3)$, confirming their equivalence.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

63186.text: If $A$ and $B$ are non-singular matrices of order 2 such that $(\mathrm{AB})^{-1}=\frac{1}{6}\left[\begin{array}{cc}-7 & -3 \\ 2 & 3\end{array}\right]$ and $\mathrm{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{3}\left[\begin{array}{cc}4 & 3 \\ -1 & 0\end{array}\right]$ then $\mathrm{B}^{-1}=$
63186.sol:
Inverse matrix computation: The inverse of the product $AB$ relates to the inverses of $A$ and $B$ by $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$.

Given $(AB)^{-1} = \frac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix}-7 & -3 \\ 2 & 3\end{bmatrix}$ and $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}4 & 3 \\ -1 & 0\end{bmatrix}$.

Multiply both sides of $(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$ on the right by $A$:

$B^{-1} = (AB)^{-1}A = \left(\frac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix}-7 & -3 \\ 2 & 3\end{bmatrix}\right)A$

To determine $A$, invert $A^{-1}$. Let $C = \begin{bmatrix}4 & 3 \\ -1 & 0\end{bmatrix}$, so $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{3}C$ and $A = 3C^{-1}$.

The determinant of $C$ is $\det(C) = 4 \cdot 0 - 3 \cdot (-1) = 3$.

The adjugate is $\operatorname{adj}(C) = \begin{bmatrix}0 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{bmatrix}$, so $C^{-1} = \frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}0 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{bmatrix}$.

Thus, $A = 3 \cdot \frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}0 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}0 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{bmatrix}$.

Substitute into the expression for $B^{-1}$:

$B^{-1} = \frac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix}-7 & -3 \\ 2 & 3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}0 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{bmatrix}$

$= \frac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix}(-7)(0) + (-3)(1) & (-7)(-3) + (-3)(4) \\ (2)(0) + (3)(1) & (2)(-3) + (3)(4)\end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix}-3 & 9 \\ 3 & 6\end{bmatrix}$

Factor: $B^{-1} = \frac{3}{6}\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$

This corresponds with option C.

63958.text: In a triangle ABC, with the usual notations, $\angle B = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$, $\angle C = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$. If D divides BC internally in the ratio 1:3, then $\dfrac{\sin \angle BAD}{\sin \angle CAD} =$
63958.sol:
Let $\angle BAD = \alpha$ and $\angle CAD = \beta$.

Applying the sine rule in $\triangle ABD$:

$\dfrac{BD}{\sin \alpha} = \dfrac{AD}{\sin B} \Rightarrow BD = \dfrac{AD \sin \alpha}{\sin B}$

Applying the sine rule in $\triangle ACD$:

$\dfrac{CD}{\sin \beta} = \dfrac{AD}{\sin C} \Rightarrow CD = \dfrac{AD \sin \beta}{\sin C}$

Dividing the two equations:

$\dfrac{BD}{CD} = \dfrac{\sin \alpha}{\sin \beta} \cdot \dfrac{\sin C}{\sin B}$

Rearranging for the required ratio:

$\dfrac{\sin \alpha}{\sin \beta} = \dfrac{BD}{CD} \cdot \dfrac{\sin B}{\sin C}$

Given that D divides BC internally in the ratio $1:3$, we have $\dfrac{BD}{CD} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

Also given $\angle B = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $\angle C = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

Substituting these values:

$\dfrac{\sin \alpha}{\sin \beta} = \dfrac{1}{3} \cdot \dfrac{\sin \left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)}{\sin \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)}$

$\dfrac{\sin \alpha}{\sin \beta} = \dfrac{1}{3} \cdot \dfrac{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}$

$\dfrac{\sin \alpha}{\sin \beta} = \dfrac{1}{3} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$

65563.subject: Physics
65563.text: In an LCR series circuit, at resonance,
options: the current and voltage are in phase
65563.sol:
In an LCR series circuit, the impedance is given by $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$.

At resonance, the inductive reactance is equal to the capacitive reactance, i.e., $X_L = X_C$.

Substituting this in the impedance formula, we get $Z = R$, which is the minimum impedance.

The phase difference $\phi$ between the voltage and current is given by $\tan \phi = \dfrac{X_L - X_C}{R}$.

Since $X_L = X_C$, $\tan \phi = 0 \Rightarrow \phi = 0$.

Therefore, the current and voltage are in phase.

Answer: the current and voltage are in phase

68655.subject: Physics
68655.text:
A particle executes a simple harmonic motion with a periodic time $8$ second. At time $t = 0$, it is at a mean position. The ratio of the distance traveled by a particle in the 2nd and that in the 1st second of its motion is
($\sin 45^{}^{\circ} = \cos 45^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, $\sin 90^{}^{\circ} = \cos 0^{}^{\circ} = 1$)
68655.sol:
The time period of the simple harmonic motion is $T = 8$ s.

The angular frequency is $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} = \dfrac{2\pi}{8} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ rad/s.

Since the particle starts from the mean position at $t = 0$, its displacement equation is given by:
$x(t) = A \sin(\omega t) = A \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} t\right)$

The distance traveled by the particle in the 1st second ($t = 0$ to $t = 1$ s) is:
$D_1 = x(1) - x(0) = A \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - 0 = \dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$

The distance traveled by the particle in the 2nd second ($t = 1$ to $t = 2$ s) is:
$D_2 = x(2) - x(1) = A \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - A \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = A - \dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$

The ratio of the distance traveled in the 2nd second to that in the 1st second is:
$\dfrac{D_2}{D_1} = \dfrac{A - \dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}}{\dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}} = \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} = \sqrt{2} - 1$

Answer: $\sqrt{2} - 1$

69418.subject: Physics
69418.text: In the following digital circuit, the output 'Y' will be '1' (one) for inputs 'A' and 'B' having values
69418.sol:
The Boolean expression for the output $Y$ can be determined from the logic circuit.

The top gate is a NAND gate with inputs $A$ and $B$. Its output is $Y_1 = \overline{A \cdot B}$.

The middle gate is a NOT gate with input $A$. Its output is $\overline{A}$.

The bottom gate is a NOR gate with inputs $\overline{A}$ and $B$. Its output is $Y_2 = \overline{\overline{A} + B}$.

The final gate is a NOR gate with inputs $Y_1$ and $Y_2$. Its output is $Y = \overline{Y_1 + Y_2}$.

Substituting the expressions for $Y_1$ and $Y_2$ into the final output equation:

$Y = \overline{\overline{A \cdot B} + \overline{\overline{A} + B}}$

Using De Morgan's laws, the expression simplifies to:

$Y = \overline{(\overline{A \cdot B})} \cdot \overline{(\overline{\overline{A} + B})}$

$Y = (A \cdot B) \cdot (\overline{A} + B)$

Expanding the expression:

$Y = A \cdot B \cdot \overline{A} + A \cdot B \cdot B$

Since $A \cdot \overline{A} = 0$ and $B \cdot B = B$, the expression becomes:

$Y = 0 + A \cdot B$

$Y = A \cdot B$

Given that the output $Y = 1$:

$A \cdot B = 1$

This condition is satisfied only when both inputs are $1$.

Therefore, $A = 1$ and $B = 1$.

Answer: $A = 1 , B = 1$

71204.text: How many spermatozoa and ova will be formed by 50 primary spermatocytes and 50 primary oocytes, respectively?
71204.sol:
During spermatogenesis, one primary spermatocyte undergoes meiosis to produce four haploid spermatozoa.

Number of spermatozoa produced by $50$ primary spermatocytes $= 50 \times 4 = 200$.

During oogenesis, one primary oocyte undergoes meiosis to produce only one functional ovum and polar bodies.

Number of ova produced by $50$ primary oocytes $= 50 \times 1 = 50$.

Thus, $200$ spermatozoa and $50$ ova will be formed.

Answer: 200 and 50

71342.subject: Biology
71342.text:
Choose the group of correct statements regarding sex-linked inheritance.
A) Y-linked genes are inherited only in males.
B) X-linked genes are inherited only in females.
C) Colourblindness shows criss-cross inheritance.
D) Haemophilia is Y-linked recessive disorder.
E) The frequency of colourblind women is much less than colourblind men.
71342.sol:
Statement A is correct. Y-linked genes (holandric genes) are present only on the Y chromosome and are inherited exclusively from father to son, thus appearing only in males.

Statement B is incorrect. X-linked genes are present on the X chromosome and are inherited by both males and females, as males have one X chromosome and females have two.

Statement C is correct. Colourblindness is an X-linked recessive trait and exhibits criss-cross inheritance, meaning it is passed from an affected father to his grandson through his carrier daughter.

Statement D is incorrect. Haemophilia is an X-linked recessive disorder, not a Y-linked disorder.

Statement E is correct. Since colourblindness is an X-linked recessive trait, a male needs only one copy of the defective gene to be affected, whereas a female needs two copies. Thus, the frequency of colourblind women is much less than that of colourblind men.

Therefore, statements A, C, and E are correct.

Answer: A, C and E only

71470.subject: Biology
71470.text: Which one of the following reactions, ADP/ATP is not involved in phosphorylation?
71470.sol:
In glycolysis, the conversion of glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate to 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate is catalyzed by the enzyme glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase.

During this step, inorganic phosphate ($P_i$) is added to the molecule, and $NAD^+$ is reduced to $NADH + H^+$. ATP or ADP is not involved in this specific phosphorylation reaction.

In contrast, the phosphorylation of glucose and fructose 6-phosphate utilizes ATP as the phosphate donor.

The conversion of 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate to 3-phosphoglycerate involves the transfer of a phosphate group to ADP, forming ATP (substrate-level phosphorylation).

Thus, ADP/ATP is not involved in the conversion of glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate to 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate.

Answer: Glyceraldehyde 3 phosphate $\rightarrow$ 1,3 biphosphoglycerate

71545.subject: Biology
71545.text: How much of water is passively absorbed by the plant?
71545.sol:
Water absorption in plants occurs through two main mechanisms: active absorption and passive absorption.

Passive absorption is driven by the transpiration pull created in the aerial parts of the plant, which pulls water upward through the xylem. This process does not require metabolic energy.

Approximately $98\%$ of the total water absorbed by a plant is taken up passively, while active absorption accounts for only about $2\%$ to $4\%$.

Answer: $98\%$

72393.sol:
The resistance of an intrinsic semiconductor decreases with an increase in temperature because more electron-hole pairs are generated, which increases conductivity.

Doping pure silicon with trivalent impurities (such as Boron, Aluminum, Gallium) creates a deficiency of electrons, leading to the formation of holes. This results in a $p$-type semiconductor.

In an $n$-type semiconductor, pentavalent impurities are added, which provide extra electrons. Therefore, the majority charge carriers in an $n$-type semiconductor are electrons, not holes.

A $p$-$n$ junction diode offers very low (negligible) resistance when it is forward biased because the width of the depletion region decreases, allowing current to flow easily.

Thus, the statement that majority carriers in $n$-type semiconductors are holes is incorrect.

Answer: The majority carries in $n$ -type semiconductors is holes

75130.subject: General Ability
75130.text: Which one of the following statements about the Bhoodan Movement is correct?
options: The target was to get one-sixth of cultivable land in India as donation
It was approved through a Central Government Act
It was ensured that the donated land was free from all litigation
The first donation of land was in Bihar
75130.sol:
The Bhoodan Movement was initiated by Acharya Vinoba Bhave in 1951 at Pochampally village in Telangana (then part of Hyderabad State). Thus, the first donation of land was not in Bihar.

The movement was a voluntary land reform initiative, and Vinoba Bhave appealed to landowners to consider him as their sixth son and donate one-sixth of their cultivable land for distribution among the landless. The target was to collect 50 million acres, which was roughly one-sixth of India's total cultivable land at the time.

The movement was not approved through a Central Government Act; rather, various state governments later passed their own Bhoodan Acts to facilitate the legal transfer of donated lands.

A significant portion of the donated land was either uncultivable or entangled in legal disputes, meaning it was not ensured that the donated land was free from litigation.

Therefore, the only correct statement is that the target was to get one-sixth of the cultivable land in India as a donation.

Answer: The target was to get one-sixth of cultivable land in India as donation

77700.subject: Mathematics
77700.text: Let $A$ and $B$ be two square matrices of same order. If $A B$ is a null matrix, then which one of the following is correct?
options: Both A and B are null matrices
Either A or B is a null matrix
B is a null matrix if A is a non-singular matrix
77700.sol:
We have, $\mathrm{AB}=0$
Let $A=\left[\begin{array}{ll}a & b \\ c & d\end{array}\right]$ and $B=\left[\begin{array}{ll}p & q \\ r & s\end{array}\right]$
So, $\mathrm{AB}=\left[\begin{array}{ll}\mathrm{a} & \mathrm{b} \\ \mathrm{c} & \mathrm{d}\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}\mathrm{p} & \mathrm{q} \\ \mathrm{r} & \mathrm{s}\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{ll}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\Rightarrow\left[\begin{array}{ll}
\mathrm{ap}+\mathrm{br} & \mathrm{aq}+\mathrm{bs} \\
\mathrm{cp}+\mathrm{dr} & \mathrm{cq}+\mathrm{ds}
\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{ll}
0 & 0 \\
0 & 0
\end{array}\right]$
Comparing both sides, we have
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{ap}+\mathrm{br}=0 ....(i)\\
& \mathrm{aq}+\mathrm{bs}=0 ....(ii)\\
& \mathrm{cp}+\mathrm{dr}=0 ....(iii)\\
& \mathrm{cq}+\mathrm{ds}=0 ....(iv)
\end{aligned}$
Solving equation (i) and (iii), we get
$(\mathrm{ad}-\mathrm{bc}) \mathrm{p}=0$ and $(\mathrm{ad}-\mathrm{bc}) \mathrm{r}=0$
Solving equation (ii) amd (iv), we get
$(\mathrm{ad}-\mathrm{bc}) \mathrm{q}=0 \text{ and }(\mathrm{ad}-\mathrm{bc}) \mathrm{s}=0$
Now, If A is non-singular $\Rightarrow \mathrm{ad}-\mathrm{bc} \neq 0$.
So, we get, $p=q=r=s=0$
So, B is a null matrix.

82522.subject: Physics
82522.text: A proton and an $\alpha$-particle are accelerated from rest to the same energy. The de-Broglie wavelengths $\lambda_p$ and $\lambda_\alpha$ are in the ratio
82522.sol:
The de-Broglie wavelength associated with a charged particle is given by
$$
\lambda=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{p}}
$$
where, $\mathrm{h}=$ planck's constant and $\mathrm{p}=$ momentum $=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mKE}}$ (here, KE is the kinetic energy of the charged particle)
$$
\Rightarrow \quad \lambda=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mKE}}}
$$
For proton and $\alpha$-particle, the wavelengths are respectively given as,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\lambda_{\mathrm{p}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{p}} \mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{p}}}} \text{ and } \lambda_\alpha=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{~m}_\alpha \mathrm{KE}_\alpha}} \\
\therefore \quad \quad \frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{p}}}{\lambda_\alpha}=\frac{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{~m}_\alpha \mathrm{KE}_\alpha}}{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{p}} \mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{P}}}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $\mathrm{KE}_\alpha=\mathrm{KE}_{\mathrm{p}}$ and $\mathrm{m}_\alpha=4 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{p}}$
Substituting these above mentioned relations in Eq. (i), we get
$$
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{P}}}{\lambda_\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{4 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{P}}}{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}}}=\frac{2}{1} \quad \text{ or } \quad \lambda_{\mathrm{P}}: \lambda_\alpha=2: 1
$$

83566.text: The voltage gain of an amplifier with $9 \%$ negative feedback is 10. The voltage gain without feedback will be
83566.sol:
The process of injecting a fraction of output energy of some device back to the input is known as feedback. When the feedback energy (voltage or current) is out of phase with the input signal and thus opposes it, it is called negative feedback.
Voltage gain with feedback is
$A_{v f}=\frac{A_\nu}{1+\beta A_\nu}$
where $A_\psi$ is voltage gain without feedback and $\beta$ is negative feedback.
Given $A_{v f}=10, \beta=9 \%=\frac{9}{100} \begin{array}{ll}
\therefore & 10=\frac{A_\nu}{1+\frac{9}{100} A_\nu} \\
\text{or } & 10+\frac{9}{10} A_\nu=A_\nu \\
\text{or } & 0.1 A_\nu=10 \text{ or } A_\nu=100
\end{array}$

84080.subject: Zoology
84080.text: The figure shows a human blood cell. Identify it and give its characteristics.
options: $\begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline \begin{array}{l}\text{ B-lymphocyte } \\ \text{ cells }$\end{array} & \begin{array}{l}$\text{ Forms about }$ 20 \% \\ $\text{$ of blood involved } \\ $\text{ immune }$\end{array} \\ \hline \end{array}
$\begin{array}{|l|l|} \hline \text{ Neutrophil } & \begin{array}{l}\text{ Most abundant } \\ \text{ blood cells }, \\ \text{ phagocytic }\end{array} \\ \hline \end{array}$
$\begin{array}{|l|l|} \hline \text{ Monocyte } & \begin{array}{l}\text{ Life span of } 3 \\ \text{ days, produces } \\ \text{ antibodies }\end{array} \\ \hline \end{array}$
84080.sol:
Basophils have three lobed nucleus and a smaller number of coarse granules. They secrete histamine, serotonin, heparin, etc., and are involved in inflammatory reactions. Lymphocytes are smaller in size having round nucleus. They are of two major types - ' $B$ ' and ' $T$ ' lymphocytes. Both $\mathrm{B}$ and $T$ lymphocytes are responsible for immune responses of the body. Neutrophils are the most abundant cells and are phagocytic in nature which destroy foreign organisms entering the body. They are polymorphic and have multi-lobed nucleus. Monocytes are the largest of all WBCs. They are motile, phagocytic in nature. Their life span is about $10-20 \mathrm{hrs}$.
Related Theory There are two types of $W B C$ - granulocytes and agranulocytes. Neutrophils, eosinophils and basophils are different types of granulocytes, while lymphocytes and monocytes are the Agranulocytes.

84594.subject: Zoology
84594.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Ovulation is caused by LH surge leading to rupture of Graafian follicles.
Statement II : Graafian follicle remaining after ovulation transform into corpus luteum and secretes large amount of estrogen.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
84594.sol:
Statement I is correct because the rapid secretion of Luteinizing Hormone (LH) leading to its maximum level during the mid-cycle (LH surge) induces the rupture of the Graafian follicle, which causes the release of the ovum (ovulation).

Statement II is incorrect because after ovulation, the ruptured Graafian follicle transforms into the corpus luteum. The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone, not estrogen, which is essential for the maintenance of the endometrium for a potential pregnancy.

Therefore, Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

95370.text:
Which of the following phylum possess multicellular, organ grade level of organisation?

1.& Platyhelminthes

2.& Porifera

3.& Nematode

4.& Protozoa
95370.sol: Though all members of Animalia are multicellular, all of them do not exhibit the same pattern of organisation of cells. For example, in sponges, the cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates, i.e., they exhibit cellular level of organisation. In coelenterates, the arrangement of cells is more complex. Here the cells performing the same function are arranged into tissues, hence is called tissue level of organisation. Organ level is exhibited by members of Platyhelminthes and other higher phyla where tissues are grouped together to form organs, each specialised for a particular function.

The brown algae group, Phaeophyceae, is primarily found in the marine habitats and show a lot of variation in size and form. They possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids, and xanthophylls. Rhodophyceae is a group of algae, also called as red algae. They are majorly found in the marine habitat having a warmer climate. They are red in color due to a higher concentration of red pigment, r-phycoerythrin in their body. They also have chlorophyll a and d. Food is stored as Floridian starch similar to amylopectin and glycogen. They generally reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation.

Chlorophyceae, also known as green algae, have a plant body that may be unicellular, colonial, or filamentous. They appear grass green in colour due to the dominance of pigments chlorophyll a and b. The majority of them have storage bodies called pyrenoids in chloroplasts.

98197.subject: Chemistry
98197.text: Organic compound firmly bound to an apoenzyme to make it catalytically active is
98197.sol:
Cofactors are the non-protein constituents that bound to an enzyme to make it catalytically active.

Cofactors can be of 3 types:
$1.$ Prosthetic groups: Organic compound firmly bound to an apoenzyme, e.g., haem is a prosthetic group for peroxidase and catalase which mediates the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen.

$2.$ Coenzymes: Organic compound loosely bound to an apoenzyme, e.g., most of the members of the vitamin B complex. Coenzymes NAD (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) and NADP (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate) contain vitamin niacin.

$3.$ Metal ions: These form coordination bonds with the side chains at the active site of the enzyme and simultaneously with 1 or more coordination bonds with the substrate, e.g., zinc act as a cofactor for carboxypeptidase enzyme.

98491.subject: Chemistry
98491.text: Which amongst the following, is a competitive inhibitor of succinic dehydrogenase?
98491.sol: When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor. Due to its close structural similarity with the substrate, the inhibitor competes with the substrate for the substrate binding site of the enzyme. Consequently, the substrate cannot bind and as a result, the enzyme action declines, e.g., inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate which closely resembles the substrate succinate in structure. Such competitive inhibitors are often used in the control of bacterial pathogens.

101413.subject: Physics
101413.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If the distance of the Earth from the Sun were suddenly reduced to half its present value, the number of days in a year would become approximately $129$.

Reason (R): The time period of revolution of a planet is directly proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of its elliptical orbit.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
101413.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: Let the initial distance be $\mathrm{r}_1 = \mathrm{r}$ and initial time period be $\mathrm{T}_1 = 365$ days.

If the distance is reduced to half, $\mathrm{r}_2 = \dfrac{\mathrm{r}}{2}$.

According to Kepler's third law, $\mathrm{T}^2 \propto \mathrm{r}^3$.

$\left(\dfrac{\mathrm{T}_2}{\mathrm{T}_1}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{\mathrm{r}_2}{\mathrm{r}_1}\right)^3$

$\dfrac{\mathrm{T}_2}{365} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3/2} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$

$\mathrm{T}_2 = \dfrac{365}{2 \times 1.414} \approx \dfrac{365}{2.828} \approx 129$ days.

Reason (R) is false: Kepler's third law states that the square of the time period of revolution ($\mathrm{T}^2$) is directly proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis ($\mathrm{r}^3$), not the time period itself.

Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

102887.subject: Physics
102887.text:
A spherical conductor has a total surface area of $4\pi \times 10^{-2}\text{ m}^2$ and a uniform surface charge density of $\dfrac{2}{\pi}\text{ \mu C m}^{-2}$. What is the magnitude of the electric field at a distance of $0.3\text{ m}$ from the centre of the sphere?
$\left(\dfrac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9\text{ N m}^2\text{ C}^{-2}\right)$
102887.sol:
First, find the total charge $Q$ on the spherical conductor by multiplying the surface charge density $\sigma$ by the surface area $A$:

$Q = \sigma \times A = \left(\dfrac{2}{\pi} \times 10^{-6}\text{ C m}^{-2}\right) \times \left(4\pi \times 10^{-2}\text{ m}^2\right) = 8 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}$

The radius of the sphere $R$ can be found from the surface area $A = 4\pi R^2$:

$4\pi R^2 = 4\pi \times 10^{-2} \Rightarrow R = 0.1\text{ m}$

Since the given distance $r = 0.3\text{ m}$ is greater than $R$, the point lies outside the sphere. The electric field is calculated assuming the entire charge is concentrated at the centre:

$E = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \dfrac{Q}{r^2}$

$E = \dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times 8 \times 10^{-8}}{(0.3)^2}$

$E = \dfrac{720}{0.09} = 8000\text{ N C}^{-1} = 8 \times 10^3\text{ N C}^{-1}$

Answer: $8 \times 10^3\text{ N C}^{-1}$

104869.subject: Physics
104869.text:
An electron in a hydrogen atom is revolving in an orbit at a radial distance of approximately $2.12 \times 10^{-10}$ m from the nucleus. The kinetic energy of the electron in this state is approximately :
(Take $1$ eV $= 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ J, $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C and $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^{9}$ N m$^2$/C$^2$)
104869.sol:
The kinetic energy $K$ of an electron in a hydrogen atom is given by the formula:
$K = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{e^2}{2r}$

Substituting the given values to find the energy in Joules:
$K = \dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19})^2}{2 \times 2.12 \times 10^{-10}}$

$K = \dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times 2.56 \times 10^{-38}}{4.24 \times 10^{-10}}$

$K = \dfrac{23.04 \times 10^{-29}}{4.24 \times 10^{-10}} \approx 5.43 \times 10^{-19}$ J

To convert this energy into electron-volts (eV), divide by $1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ J/eV:
$K = \dfrac{5.43 \times 10^{-19}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}} \approx 3.4$ eV

Note: The total energy is $-3.4$ eV, and the potential energy is $-6.8$ eV. Kinetic energy is always positive and equal in magnitude to the total energy.

Answer: $3.4$ eV

105110.text: A nucleus ${ }_Z^A X$ has mass represented by $m(A, Z)$. If $m_p$ and $m_n$ denote the mass of proton and neutron respectively and $B E$ the binding energy (in MeV ) then,
105110.sol:
In the case of formation of nucleus the evolution of energy equals to the binding energy of the nucleus takes place due to disappearance of a fraction of total mass. If the quantity of mass disappearing is $\Delta m$, then the binding energy is
$B E=\Delta m c^2$
cFrom the above discussion, it is clear that the mass of the nucleus must be less than the sum of the masses of the constituent neutrons and protons. We can then write
$\Delta m=Z m_p-N m_n-m(A, Z)$
where $m(A, Z)$ is the mass of the atom of mass number $A$ atomic number $Z$. Hence, the binding energy of nucleus is
$\begin{aligned} & B E=\left[Z m_p+N m_n-m(A, Z)\right] c^2 \\ & B E=\left[Z m_p+(A-Z) m_n-m(A, Z)\right] c^2\end{aligned}$

105233.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the behaviour of circuits containing two identical ideal $p-n$ junction diodes connected to a DC source.

List-I (Configuration)List-II (Circuit Behaviour)
(A) Two diodes in series, both forward-biased(I) High equivalent resistance, unequal potential drops across the diodes
(B) Two diodes in series, both reverse-biased(II) Low equivalent resistance, current flows almost entirely through one diode
(C) Two diodes in series, one forward-biased and one reverse-biased(III) Low equivalent resistance, equal potential drops across the diodes
(D) Two diodes in parallel, one forward-biased and one reverse-biased(IV) High equivalent resistance, equal potential drops across the diodes


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
105233.sol:
In configuration (A), both diodes are forward-biased, offering low resistance. Being identical, they have equal resistance and thus equal potential drops. (A) matches (III).

In configuration (B), both diodes are reverse-biased, offering very high resistance. Being identical, they have equal high resistance and equal potential drops. (B) matches (IV).

In configuration (C), one diode is forward-biased (low resistance) and one is reverse-biased (high resistance). The equivalent resistance of the series combination is high. The potential drop is proportional to resistance, so it is unequal (mostly across the reverse-biased diode). (C) matches (I).

In configuration (D), the forward-biased diode offers low resistance and the reverse-biased diode offers high resistance in parallel. The equivalent resistance is low (slightly less than the forward-biased diode's resistance). Current takes the path of least resistance, flowing almost entirely through the forward-biased diode. (D) matches (II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

106985.subject: Chemistry
106985.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
106985.text: Consider the elements Nitrogen (N), Oxygen (O), and Fluorine (F). Which of the following options correctly represents the increasing order of their electronegativity and their first ionization enthalpy?
106985.sol:
Electronegativity generally increases across a period from left to right due to an increase in effective nuclear charge. Therefore, the correct increasing order of electronegativity for these Period 2 elements is $\mathrm{N} \lt \mathrm{O} \lt \mathrm{F}$.

First ionization enthalpy also generally increases across a period, but there is an exception between Group 15 and Group 16. Nitrogen (Group 15) has a stable half-filled $2p$ subshell ($2s^{2} 2p^{3}$), whereas Oxygen (Group 16) has a $2s^{2} 2p^{4}$ configuration. Removing an electron from the stable half-filled orbitals of nitrogen requires more energy than removing an electron from oxygen. Hence, the first ionization enthalpy of nitrogen is higher than that of oxygen. Fluorine has the highest first ionization enthalpy among the three. Thus, the correct increasing order for first ionization enthalpy is $\mathrm{O} \lt \mathrm{N} \lt \mathrm{F}$.

Answer: Electronegativity: $\mathrm{N} \lt \mathrm{O} \lt \mathrm{F}$ ; First ionization enthalpy: $\mathrm{O} \lt \mathrm{N} \lt \mathrm{F}$

107731.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The $\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bond angle in water is smaller than the $\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}$ bond angle in ammonia.

Reason (R): The oxygen atom in water possesses two lone pairs of electrons, resulting in greater lone pair - lone pair repulsion which compresses the bond angle more than the single lone pair in ammonia.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
107731.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct: The bond angle in water ($\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$) is $104.5^\circ$, which is smaller than the bond angle in ammonia ($\mathrm{NH}_3$), which is $107^\circ$.

Reason (R) is also correct and explains (A): Both central atoms (O in $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ and N in $\mathrm{NH}_3$) are $sp^3$ hybridized. However, oxygen has two lone pairs while nitrogen has only one. According to VSEPR theory, the order of repulsive interactions is lone pair - lone pair $>$ lone pair - bond pair $>$ bond pair - bond pair. The strong lone pair - lone pair repulsion in water pushes the $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds closer together, compressing the angle more than the single lone pair does in ammonia.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

112648.subject: Chemistry
112648.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The heavy organic liquid obtained by the reaction of acetophenone with sodium hypochlorite produces a foul-smelling compound when heated with aniline and ethanolic potassium hydroxide.
Reason (R): Acetophenone undergoes the haloform reaction with sodium hypochlorite to form chloroform, which then gives a positive carbylamine test with primary amines.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
112648.sol:
Acetophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$) contains a methyl ketone group. When treated with sodium hypochlorite ($\text{NaOCl}$), it undergoes the haloform reaction to yield sodium benzoate and chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$).

Chloroform is a heavy organic liquid. When chloroform is heated with a primary amine such as aniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$) and ethanolic potassium hydroxide, it undergoes the carbylamine reaction.

The product of the carbylamine reaction is phenyl isocyanide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NC}$), which is characterized by a highly offensive or foul smell.

Therefore, the heavy organic liquid is chloroform, and it produces a foul-smelling isocyanide upon reaction with aniline and ethanolic $\text{KOH}$.

Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true statements, and Reason (R) provides the correct chemical explanation for the observation described in Assertion (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

113879.subject: Chemistry
113879.text: $6.3\text{ g}$ of oxalic acid dihydrate ($\mathrm{H_2C_2O_4 \cdot 2H_2O}$) is dissolved in water to prepare an $\dfrac{\mathrm{M}}{10}$ aqueous solution. The volume of the resulting solution is :
113879.sol:
First, calculate the molar mass of oxalic acid dihydrate ($\mathrm{H_2C_2O_4 \cdot 2H_2O}$):
$\mathrm{Molar\ mass} = (2 \times 1) + (2 \times 12) + (4 \times 16) + 2 \times (2 \times 1 + 16)$
$\mathrm{Molar\ mass} = 2 + 24 + 64 + 36 = 126\text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Number of moles of solute ($n$):
$n = \dfrac{\text{Given mass}}{\text{Molar mass}} = \dfrac{6.3}{126} = 0.05\text{ mol}$

The given molarity is $\dfrac{\mathrm{M}}{10} = 0.1\text{ M}$.

Molarity ($\mathrm{M}$) is given by:
$\mathrm{M} = \dfrac{n}{V\text{ (in L)}}$

$0.1 = \dfrac{0.05}{V}$

$V = \dfrac{0.05}{0.1} = 0.5\text{ L}$

Converting the volume to mL:
$V = 0.5 \times 1000\text{ mL} = 500\text{ mL}$

Answer: $500\text{ mL}$

114366.subject: Chemistry
114366.text:
The standard Gibbs energy change ($\Delta_{\text{r}}G^{\ominus}$) for the following reaction is $-868.5 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ :
$2\text{M(s)} + 6\text{H}^{+}(\text{aq}) \rightarrow 2\text{M}^{3+}(\text{aq}) + 3\text{H}_{2}(\text{g})$
Calculate the standard reduction potential of the $\text{M}^{3+}/\text{M}$ half-cell.
(Given : $1 \text{ F} = 96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
114366.sol:
For the given balanced reaction, the number of moles of electrons transferred is $n = 6$.

Using the relation:
$\Delta_{\text{r}}G^{\ominus} = -nFE_{\text{cell}}^{\ominus}$
$-868500 \text{ J mol}^{-1} = -6 \times 96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1} \times E_{\text{cell}}^{\ominus}$
$E_{\text{cell}}^{\ominus} = \dfrac{868500}{579000} \text{ V} = +1.50 \text{ V}$

The cell consists of the $\text{M}$ anode and the Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE) as the cathode.
$E_{\text{cell}}^{\ominus} = E_{\text{cathode}}^{\ominus} - E_{\text{anode}}^{\ominus}$
$1.50 \text{ V} = E_{\text{H}^{+}/\text{H}_{2}}^{\ominus} - E_{\text{M}^{3+}/\text{M}}^{\ominus}$
$1.50 \text{ V} = 0 \text{ V} - E_{\text{M}^{3+}/\text{M}}^{\ominus}$
$E_{\text{M}^{3+}/\text{M}}^{\ominus} = -1.50 \text{ V}$

Answer: $-1.50 \text{ V}$
